title: Variant KV segmentation and adaptive batch-priority profiles for long-context models
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background:
We observe sustained high peak GPU memory pressure and sporadic latency spikes when serving long-context variants (>= 32k) of Llama, Mistral, and Qwen families under continuous-batching. Current slab-based allocators and monolithic KV residency policies force early full-KV materialization for many requests (high memory) or overly conservative eviction (higher P95 latency due to cache misses).

Goal:
Design and implement a model-aware KV segmentation + adaptive batch-priority profile system that reduces steady-state peak GPU memory by 10-25% for long-context variants while preserving P95 latency within SLOs and keeping throughput stable. Provide a rollout path that can be toggled per-model and per-customer (hosted/dedicated/private).

Success metrics:
- 15% median reduction in observed max GPU memory per-GPU on qwen-14b-longctx in our synthetic replay tests.
- P95 generation latency increase <= 10% vs baseline (preferably neutral).
- End-to-end token throughput (tokens/s) +/- 5% vs baseline under same commit.
- No regression in correctness or end-user visible errors.
- Gradual cost improvement signal in Optimize dashboards for long-context workloads.

Proposed approach (technical summary):
1) KV Segmentation: Define per-model and per-variant KV "segments" (logical groups of KV data) mapped to layers or contiguous parameter regions. Segments have metadata: hotness score, estimated residency bytes, and prefetch cost. Segmentation is generated by a new offline profile builder (variant-profile-generator) and shipped alongside model manifests.

2) Slabless freelist for large segments: For long-context variants, instead of forcing slab allocation for KV, use a slabless freelist allocator with per-segment freelist buckets tuned to expected allocation lifetimes. This reduces external fragmentation for large, infrequently touched segments.

3) Adaptive batch-priority profiles: Assign each incoming request a dynamic batching priority based on: model variant, requested sequence length, token position, whether the request is a prefix continuation (cacheable) or fresh, and the segment-hotness profile. The batcher then groups requests with similar priority and prefetch cost estimates to reduce redundant prefetch and allow partial-KV materialization.

4) Partial-KV materialization and lazy prefetch: When a request is first scheduled, only materialize KV segments estimated to be hot for the first N tokens (configurable per-variant). Remaining segments are fetched lazily as decoding progresses or on-demand after a low-latency background prefetch.

5) Compression & compact residency hints: Alongside segmentation, ship compact residency hints (delta-compressed, quantized occupancy maps) to let runtime cheaply estimate memory footprint of keeping a segment resident. These hints power fast admission decisions in the allocator.

Implementation notes and interfaces:
- New artifact: /profiles/variant/ENG-1200456/<model>-segment-profile.v1 (protobuf-blobs). The runtime will load these at model startup if available and fall back to generic heuristics otherwise.
- Batcher: extend continuous-batcher with priority queues and cost-estimator hooks. Add API: estimate_prefetch_cost(request_meta) -> string token (cheap codepath).
- Allocator: new slabless freelist mode flag with per-segment freelists. Controlled via model manifest: memory_profile: { mode: "freelist-v1", segment_hint_uri: "..." }.
- Telemetry: add batch_priority, prefetch_count, segments_materialized, and per-request prefetch_bytes metrics. Emit sample traces for failed predictions.

Experiment plan and benchmarks:
- Unit tests for segmentation parser, freelist correctness, and priority queue behavior.
- Microbench: run synthetic replay with 10k requests (mix of continuation vs cold starts) for each variant: llama-70b-longctx, mistral-7b-longctx, qwen-14b-longctx. Collect peak GPU memory, P50/P95 latency, and prefetch bytes.
- Canary in staging: 2 nodes per-variant with 5% traffic split, compare against control for 48 hours and run stress soak for 24 hours.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: Internal experiments & sprints (this ticket) -> feature gated off in runtime.
- Phase 1: Staging canary (per-model flag enabled) for 48-72h.
- Phase 2: Host-wide canary for low-risk models (mistral-7b-longctx) at 5-10% traffic.
- Phase 3: Expand to dedicated pools with opt-in config.
- Phase 4: Default enable for select long-context models if metrics meet thresholds.

Fallback and safety:
- Fallback flag to force baseline allocator path per-request or per-model at runtime.
- If prefetch misprediction rate > 8% (based on wasted prefetch bytes), auto-revert the segment profile for that workload and surface alert.

Monitoring and dashboards:
- New dashboard: "KV Segmentation / Prefetch" with heatmaps of segments_materialized vs time, prefetch_waste ratio, and distribution of batch_priority.
- Alert: sustained increase in P95 (> 15% over baseline) for any model variant for 10 minutes.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How to choose segment granularity: per-layer vs per-contiguous-param-range. Finer granularity reduces wasted residency but increases metadata and decision latency. We will prototype with 3 granularities and pick the knee.
- Interaction with quantized kernels: compressed residency hints may misestimate memory when quantized kernels share buffers. Add small conservatism factor per-variant.
- Cost to store and ship profiles; keep blobs small (< 200KB per-variant target).

Artifacts and references:
- Design doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Variant+KV+Segmentation+Design (draft)
- Profiling scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-profiles/tree/ENG-1200456
- Synthetic replay dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rerun/kv-segmentation-experiments
